LGEDF Single County Coal Severance

The Local Government Economic Development Fund (LGEDF), also known as “Single-County” Coal Severance, grants are available for any coal-producing county for any economic or industrial development projects as defined by KRS 42.4588.

The 2026-2028 Executive Branch Budget of the Commonwealth also allows that LGEDF grants to be allocated to projects that have the concurrence of the respective County Judge-Executive, State Representative(s) and State Senator(s).

Eligibility Criteria

The Local Government Economic Development Fund (LGEDF), also known as the Single-County Coal Severance Program, provides funding to eligible coal-producing counties for economic and industrial development projects as defined by KRS 42.4588. Projects must have the concurrence of the respective County Judge/Executive, State Representative(s), and State Senator(s) as required by current state budget provisions.

Required Documentation

Completed application, project scope and budget, authorizing resolution, legislative concurrence letters, and any additional materials required by DLG or the legislative appropriation.

Award Details

Funding is provided through the Local Government Economic Development Fund (LGEDF) as grant assistance for eligible projects. Award amounts are subject to available funding and DLG approval. Funds are reimbursed following execution of a Grant Agreement/Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and satisfaction of program requirements.

Application Process

  • Complete the LGEDF application form.

  • Prepare a project scope and budget detailing the proposed project and anticipated outcomes.

  • Obtain the required Fiscal Court resolution and legislative concurrence letters.

  • Submit the completed application package and all supporting documentation to the Department for Local Government (DLG).

  • DLG will review the application for completeness, eligibility, and compliance prior to award consideration.
